skill.name: frontend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Opinionated frontend development standards for React and TypeScript applications using Suspense, TanStack Query, TanStack Router, MUI v7, and feature-based architecture.
skill.summary: Guides React teams toward consistent TypeScript, routing, styling, data fetching, and performance patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Frontend teams often drift across data fetching, routing, styling, and TypeScript patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concrete React guidelines for predictable implementation and review.
actual_capabilities: Defines Suspense-first data fetching patterns with TanStack Query.
Gives React component structure rules for props, hooks, memoization, handlers, and exports.
Documents feature-based folder organization and import alias conventions.
Shows MUI v7 styling examples, including Grid syntax and sx organization.
Provides routing, lazy loading, loading, error, and performance checklists.
Includes complete examples for API services, cache-first queries, mutations, and route files.
limitations: It is opinionated and may conflict with existing frontend architecture.
It does not run tests, lint code, or verify bundle size by itself.
Examples assume React, TypeScript, MUI, TanStack Query, and TanStack Router.
Developers must still validate accessibility, security, and product requirements.

use_cases.title: Standardize a React Feature
use_cases.description: Use the guidance to structure feature folders, API services, queries, components, and route files consistently.

use_cases.title: Review Frontend Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Compare changes against Suspense, TypeScript, MUI, performance, and data-fetching standards before approval.

use_cases.title: Plan a Frontend Migration
use_cases.description: Create shared rules for moving a React codebase toward stricter typing and predictable feature boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines to build a typed React component for this requirement. Follow the required structure, Suspense rules, and MUI v7 styling patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines to plan and implement a new feature. Include folder structure, API service boundaries, query hooks, route placement, and component responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines to review this frontend change. Identify issues with TypeScript, imports, Suspense boundaries, data fetching, MUI usage, and performance defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines to refactor this React area toward feature-based architecture. Preserve behavior while improving boundaries, lazy loading, query usage, and maintainability.

output_examples.input: Ask for a new customer profile page with data loading and edit actions.
output_examples.output: A structured implementation plan covering route placement, feature folders, typed API methods, Suspense query hooks, component boundaries, and MUI layout choices.

output_examples.input: Ask for a review of a frontend pull request.
output: Flags early loading returns that should move behind Suspense boundaries.
Notes missing explicit TypeScript return types and unsafe import paths.
Suggests lazy loading for heavy grids and dialogs.

output_examples.input: Ask how to organize a new analytics feature.
output_examples.output: A feature-based outline with API, components, hooks, helpers, types, public exports, and route integration guidance.

best_practices: Apply the guidance before writing code, so architecture decisions are explicit.
Keep project-specific exceptions documented when existing code cannot follow the standard.
Pair the skill with tests, linting, accessibility checks, and runtime validation.
anti_patterns: Do not force these rules onto projects that use different frontend frameworks.
Do not treat sample code as a complete production implementation.
Do not skip product, accessibility, and security review because the structure looks correct.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets React applications using TypeScript, MUI v7, TanStack Query, and TanStack Router.

faq.question: Can it help with existing codebases?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide reviews and refactors, but teams should apply changes incrementally.

faq.question: Does it generate runnable frontend code?
faq.answer: It can guide code generation, but it does not execute, test, or deploy the code.

faq.question: Is Suspense required for every data fetch?
faq.answer: The skill strongly prefers Suspense for new components and treats legacy patterns as exceptions.

faq.question: Does it cover styling decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes MUI v7 Grid syntax, sx usage, and guidance for separate style files.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it for reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
